payload.text:
I found one critical bug: the branch doesn't actually merge overlapping imports. As you asked, I didn't change any files.

**CRITICAL**
- `src/dedupe.js:2`: `[...new Set(contacts)]` removes duplicates only when they're the exact same object in memory. Two imports that overlap give you separate objects that share an id, so both are kept. The README says the opposite: "Identity is the id, never object identity." I ran `mergeImports([{id:1,name:'Ada'}], [{id:1,name:'Ada'}])` and got both contacts back.
  Fix: go by id and keep the first one seen, e.g. `const seen = new Set(); return contacts.filter(c => !seen.has(c.id) && seen.add(c.id));`

**INFORMATIONAL**
- `test/dedupe.test.js:5`: the tests pass because they only check the same object listed twice, which the current code handles. Nothing tests two separate objects with the same id, and nothing tests `mergeImports` at all.
  Fix: add a test where `dedupe([{id:1,name:'Ada'}, {id:1,name:'Ada B'}])` returns only the first contact, plus one test that merges two overlapping lists with `mergeImports`.

`src/order.js` and the README, CHANGELOG and version changes look fine.
